templates.name: Docker host
templates.summary: An Ubuntu VM running the Docker engine and the compose plugin, with the default user in the docker group; ports 8080 and 8443 and the Docker socket are forwarded to the host.
templates.compose:
name: dockerhost
services:
  docker:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 40          # GiB
    nested: true
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
      - "8443:8443"
    sockets:
      - "~/.docker/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "4"
          memory: 4096M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - docker.io
      - docker-compose-v2
    post_commands:
      - systemctl enable --now docker
      - usermod -aG docker ubuntu
    write_files:
      - path: /etc/motd.d/dockerhost.motd
        content: |
          Docker is ready. Ports 8080 and 8443 of this VM are forwarded to the host:
          publish a container on one of them (docker run -p 8080:80 ...) to reach it on localhost.
          The Docker socket is forwarded to ~/.docker/run/docker.sock on the host: use it with
          `export DOCKER_HOST=unix://$HOME/.docker/run/docker.sock` (it gives root-equivalent access to this VM).
        permissions: "0644"

templates.name: k3s Kubernetes (single node)
templates.summary: A single-node k3s cluster; the Kubernetes API is forwarded to the host on port 6443, and the ingress (Traefik) on 8080 and 8443.
templates.compose:
name: k3s
services:
  server:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 30          # GiB
    ports:
      - "6443:6443"
      - "8080:80"
      - "8443:443"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 4096M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - curl
    write_files:
      - path: /etc/motd.d/k3s.motd
        content: |
          k3s is running. The kubeconfig is /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml: copy it to the host and
          point its `server:` at this VM's address (or at localhost, port 6443 is forwarded).
          The ingress controller answers on this VM's ports 80 and 443, forwarded to the host's 8080 and 8443.
        permissions: "0644"
    post_commands:
      # The installer script is downloaded from get.k3s.io: read it before running this on anything that matters.
      - curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | K3S_KUBECONFIG_MODE=644 sh -

templates.name: MariaDB + phpMyAdmin
templates.summary: A MariaDB server and a phpMyAdmin web UI on a second VM that finds it through compose DNS.
templates.compose:
# compose.yml — Caker multi-VM environment (docker compose compatible)
# Run `cakectl compose up` to start all services in depends_on order.
# Run `cakectl compose down` to stop them in reverse order.
# Run `cakectl compose ps` to show their status.
# Run `cakectl compose init` to regenerate this file.
name: myapp
services:
  # MariaDB — real package install (via `packages:`) plus first-boot setup (via `post_commands:`),
  # pulling its admin password/DB name straight out of `environment:` rather than hardcoding them
  # a second time — a demo of all three fields working together. (Not PostgreSQL/pgAdmin: pgAdmin's
  # apt repo publishes amd64 packages only, no arm64 build, which made that pairing unusable on
  # Apple Silicon hosts — MariaDB/phpMyAdmin are both in Ubuntu's own default repos for every arch.)
  mariadb:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    ports:
      - "3306:3306"
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: secret
      MYSQL_DATABASE: myapp
      # Dedicated account (granted on MYSQL_DATABASE only) to log in to phpMyAdmin with.
      MYSQL_USER: myapp
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: myapp-secret
    networks:
      - default
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2048M
    # Caker VM extensions:
    disk: 20          # GiB
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    nested: true
    disk_format: raw
    dynamic_port_forwarding: false
    ifnames: true
    package_upgrade: true
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - mariadb-server
    post_commands:
      - sed -i "s/^bind-address.*/bind-address = 0.0.0.0/" /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf
      - systemctl restart mariadb
      # Runs before the root password is set below, while root can still log in over the unix socket.
      - mysql -u root -e "CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS '$(grep ^MYSQL_USER= /etc/environment | cut -d= -f2)'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '$(grep ^MYSQL_PASSWORD= /etc/environment | cut -d= -f2)'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON $(grep ^MYSQL_DATABASE= /etc/environment | cut -d= -f2).* TO '$(grep ^MYSQL_USER= /etc/environment | cut -d= -f2)'@'%'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"
      - mysql -u root -e "ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '$(grep MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD /etc/environment | cut -d= -f2)'; CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS $(grep MYSQL_DATABASE /etc/environment | cut -d= -f2); GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO 'root'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '$(grep MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD /etc/environment | cut -d= -f2)' WITH GRANT OPTION; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"

  # phpMyAdmin (web) — the phpmyadmin package is debconf-interactive by default (which webserver to
  # auto-configure, whether to run its own local dbconfig-common setup) and would hang waiting for
  # prompts under cloud-init's non-interactive `packages:` install — unlike mariadb above, this has
  # to preseed those answers via `post_commands:` before installing, same "packages: only works
  # when nothing needs asking first" lesson the old pgAdmin pairing demonstrated.
  phpmyadmin:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    networks:
      - default
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 1024M
    disk: 10          # GiB
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    nested: true
    disk_format: raw
    dynamic_port_forwarding: false
    ifnames: true
    package_upgrade: true
    package_update: true
    environment:
      PMA_HOST: mariadb.myapp.compose.internal   # the mariadb VM's compose DNS name; preselects it on the login form
    depends_on:
      - mariadb
    write_files:
      - path: /etc/motd.d/phpmyadmin.motd
        content: |
          phpMyAdmin is reachable at http://<this-vm-ip>/phpmyadmin (forwarded to host port 8080).
          Log in with the mariadb service's MYSQL_USER/MYSQL_PASSWORD (or root/MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD),
          and the mariadb VM's IP as the server unless PMA_HOST is set — find it with
          `cakectl infos compose-myapp-mariadb`.
        permissions: "0644"
      # Debian's phpMyAdmin only talks to `localhost` by default. Point it at PMA_HOST when set,
      # otherwise let the login form accept any server address.
      - path: /etc/phpmyadmin/conf.d/caker.inc.php
        content: |
          <?php
          $caker_env = @parse_ini_file('/etc/phpmyadmin/caker.env', false, INI_SCANNER_RAW) ?: [];
          if (!empty($caker_env['PMA_HOST'])) {
              $cfg['Servers'][1]['host'] = $caker_env['PMA_HOST'];
          } else {
              $cfg['AllowArbitraryServer'] = true;
          }
        permissions: "0644"
      # - path: /etc/myapp/app.conf  # `source:` reads a file from the host instead of inlining it
      #   source: ./app.conf         # resolved relative to the current directory, like `volumes:`
    post_commands:
      - echo "phpmyadmin phpmyadmin/dbconfig-install boolean false" | debconf-set-selections
      - echo "phpmyadmin phpmyadmin/reconfigure-webserver multiselect apache2" | debconf-set-selections
      - DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y phpmyadmin
      - a2enconf phpmyadmin
      # phpMyAdmin's apache open_basedir can't read /etc/environment, so copy the PMA_* values next to its config.
      - grep '^PMA_' /etc/environment > /etc/phpmyadmin/caker.env || true
      - chown root:www-data /etc/phpmyadmin/caker.env && chmod 0640 /etc/phpmyadmin/caker.env
      - systemctl reload apache2

networks:
  default:
    driver: bridge

templates.name: PostgreSQL
templates.summary: PostgreSQL from the Ubuntu archive, listening on every interface with an application role and database.
templates.compose:
name: postgres
services:
  db:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 20          # GiB
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: change-me
      POSTGRES_DB: app
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2048M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - postgresql
      - postgresql-contrib
    post_commands:
      - sed -i "s/^#\?listen_addresses.*/listen_addresses = '*'/" /etc/postgresql/*/main/postgresql.conf
      - echo "host all all 0.0.0.0/0 scram-sha-256" >> /etc/postgresql/*/main/pg_hba.conf
      - systemctl restart postgresql
      # The values come from `environment:` above (written to /etc/environment).
      - |
        . /etc/environment
        su postgres -c "psql -c \"CREATE ROLE $POSTGRES_USER LOGIN PASSWORD '$POSTGRES_PASSWORD'\""
        su postgres -c "createdb -O $POSTGRES_USER $POSTGRES_DB"

templates.name: Redis
templates.summary: Redis from the Ubuntu archive, reachable from the host and from the other VMs, protected by a password.
templates.compose:
name: redis
services:
  redis:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 10          # GiB
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: change-me
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 1024M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - redis-server
    post_commands:
      - sed -i 's/^bind .*/bind 0.0.0.0 -::*/' /etc/redis/redis.conf
      - |
        . /etc/environment
        echo "requirepass $REDIS_PASSWORD" >> /etc/redis/redis.conf
      - systemctl restart redis-server

templates.name: RabbitMQ
templates.summary: RabbitMQ with the management UI; AMQP is forwarded on 5672 and the web console on 15672.
templates.compose:
name: rabbitmq
services:
  broker:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 10          # GiB
    ports:
      - "5672:5672"
      - "15672:15672"
    environment:
      RABBITMQ_USER: admin
      RABBITMQ_PASSWORD: change-me
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2048M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - rabbitmq-server
    post_commands:
      - systemctl enable --now rabbitmq-server
      - rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_management
      - |
        . /etc/environment
        rabbitmqctl add_user "$RABBITMQ_USER" "$RABBITMQ_PASSWORD"
        rabbitmqctl set_user_tags "$RABBITMQ_USER" administrator
        rabbitmqctl set_permissions -p / "$RABBITMQ_USER" ".*" ".*" ".*"

templates.name: LAMP stack
templates.summary: Apache with PHP on one VM and MariaDB on another, wired together through compose DNS.
templates.compose:
name: lamp
services:
  db:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 20          # GiB
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: app
      MYSQL_USER: app
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: change-me
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2048M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - mariadb-server
    post_commands:
      - sed -i "s/^bind-address.*/bind-address = 0.0.0.0/" /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf
      - systemctl restart mariadb
      - |
        . /etc/environment
        mysql -u root -e "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS $MYSQL_DATABASE; CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS '$MYSQL_USER'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '$MYSQL_PASSWORD'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON $MYSQL_DATABASE.* TO '$MYSQL_USER'@'%'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"

  web:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 10          # GiB
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    depends_on:
      - db
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 1024M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - apache2
      - libapache2-mod-php
      - php-mysql
    write_files:
      # `db.lamp.compose.internal` is the db service's compose DNS name (<service>.<project>.<domain>).
      - path: /var/www/html/index.php
        content: |
          <?php
          $db = @new mysqli('db.lamp.compose.internal', 'app', 'change-me', 'app');
          echo $db->connect_errno ? 'Database: ' . $db->connect_error : 'Database: connected, MariaDB ' . $db->server_info;
          echo '<hr>';
          phpinfo();
        permissions: "0644"
    post_commands:
      - rm -f /var/www/html/index.html
      - systemctl restart apache2

templates.name: LEMP stack
templates.summary: Nginx with PHP-FPM on one VM and MariaDB on another, wired together through compose DNS.
templates.compose:
name: lemp
services:
  db:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 20          # GiB
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: app
      MYSQL_USER: app
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: change-me
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2048M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - mariadb-server
    post_commands:
      - sed -i "s/^bind-address.*/bind-address = 0.0.0.0/" /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/50-server.cnf
      - systemctl restart mariadb
      - |
        . /etc/environment
        mysql -u root -e "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS $MYSQL_DATABASE; CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS '$MYSQL_USER'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY '$MYSQL_PASSWORD'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON $MYSQL_DATABASE.* TO '$MYSQL_USER'@'%'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"

  web:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 10          # GiB
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    depends_on:
      - db
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 1024M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - nginx
      - php-fpm
      - php-mysql
    write_files:
      # Staged outside /etc/nginx so the package's own default site can't clash with it; copied in below.
      - path: /root/lemp-site.conf
        content: |
          server {
              listen 80 default_server;
              root /var/www/html;
              index index.php index.html;
              location / { try_files $uri $uri/ =404; }
              location ~ \.php$ {
                  include snippets/fastcgi-php.conf;
                  fastcgi_pass unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock;
              }
          }
        permissions: "0644"
      # `db.lemp.compose.internal` is the db service's compose DNS name (<service>.<project>.<domain>).
      - path: /var/www/html/index.php
        content: |
          <?php
          $db = @new mysqli('db.lemp.compose.internal', 'app', 'change-me', 'app');
          echo $db->connect_errno ? 'Database: ' . $db->connect_error : 'Database: connected, MariaDB ' . $db->server_info;
          echo '<hr>';
          phpinfo();
        permissions: "0644"
    post_commands:
      - cp /root/lemp-site.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/default
      - nginx -t && systemctl restart nginx

templates.name: Node.js + Redis
templates.summary: A small Node.js HTTP app (hit counter) running as a systemd service, backed by a Redis VM.
templates.compose:
name: nodeapp
services:
  cache:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 10          # GiB
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "1"
          memory: 1024M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - redis-server
    post_commands:
      # Development setup: Redis answers every VM on the network without a password.
      - sed -i 's/^bind .*/bind 0.0.0.0 -::*/' /etc/redis/redis.conf
      - sed -i 's/^protected-mode yes/protected-mode no/' /etc/redis/redis.conf
      - systemctl restart redis-server

  app:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 10          # GiB
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    depends_on:
      - cache
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 1024M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - nodejs
      - npm
    write_files:
      - path: /opt/app/package.json
        content: |
          { "name": "app", "version": "1.0.0", "private": true, "dependencies": { "redis": "^4.7.0" } }
        permissions: "0644"
      # `cache.nodeapp.compose.internal` is the cache service's compose DNS name (<service>.<project>.<domain>).
      - path: /opt/app/server.js
        content: |
          const http = require('http');
          const { createClient } = require('redis');
          const redis = createClient({ url: 'redis://cache.nodeapp.compose.internal:6379' });
          redis.connect().then(() => {
            http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
              const hits = await redis.incr('hits');
              res.end(`Hello from Node.js, ${hits} hits\n`);
            }).listen(3000);
          });
        permissions: "0644"
      - path: /etc/systemd/system/app.service
        content: |
          [Unit]
          Description=Node.js app
          After=network-online.target

          [Service]
          WorkingDirectory=/opt/app
          ExecStart=/usr/bin/node server.js
          Restart=on-failure

          [Install]
          WantedBy=multi-user.target
        permissions: "0644"
    post_commands:
      - cd /opt/app && npm install --omit=dev
      - systemctl daemon-reload
      - systemctl enable --now app

templates.name: Python (Flask) + PostgreSQL
templates.summary: A small Flask app (hit counter) running as a systemd service, backed by a PostgreSQL VM.
templates.compose:
name: pyapp
services:
  db:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 20          # GiB
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: change-me
      POSTGRES_DB: app
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2048M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - postgresql
    post_commands:
      - sed -i "s/^#\?listen_addresses.*/listen_addresses = '*'/" /etc/postgresql/*/main/postgresql.conf
      - echo "host all all 0.0.0.0/0 scram-sha-256" >> /etc/postgresql/*/main/pg_hba.conf
      - systemctl restart postgresql
      - |
        . /etc/environment
        su postgres -c "psql -c \"CREATE ROLE $POSTGRES_USER LOGIN PASSWORD '$POSTGRES_PASSWORD'\""
        su postgres -c "createdb -O $POSTGRES_USER $POSTGRES_DB"

  app:
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    user: ubuntu
    password: ubuntu
    disk: 10          # GiB
    ports:
      - "5000:5000"
    depends_on:
      - db
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 1024M
    package_update: true
    packages:
      - python3-flask
      - python3-psycopg2
    write_files:
      # `db.pyapp.compose.internal` is the db service's compose DNS name (<service>.<project>.<domain>).
      - path: /opt/app/app.py
        content: |
          import psycopg2
          from flask import Flask

          app = Flask(__name__)

          def connection():
              return psycopg2.connect(host="db.pyapp.compose.internal", user="app", password="change-me", dbname="app")

          @app.route("/")
          def index():
              with connection() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
                  cur.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hits (n integer)")
                  cur.execute("INSERT INTO hits VALUES (1)")
                  cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM hits")
                  return "Hello from Flask, %d hits\n" % cur.fetchone()[0]

          app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000)
        permissions: "0644"
      - path: /etc/systemd/system/app.service
        content: |
          [Unit]
          Description=Flask app
          After=network-online.target

          [Service]
          WorkingDirectory=/opt/app
          ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 app.py
          Restart=on-failure

          [Install]
          WantedBy=multi-user.target
        permissions: "0644"
    post_commands:
      - systemctl daemon-reload
      - systemctl enable --now app
